TRACK READY

How we cover the two days

A private event, told publicly. Two days at the Autodrome turned into something the whole audience gets to follow, without publishing a single guest list.

Closer to a camera roll than to event coverage. Quick, playful, shot from inside the day rather than from the sidelines.

And while that runs, we shoot in parallel. Two days on a circuit is the cheapest chance we will get to bank MINI content made here, on track, with regional plates and a regional skyline. That material carries the account long after the weekend is over.

01

The thought

The event is already built as a test facility. The account simply becomes part of it.

For two days, the account is the timing screen.

Not a page posting about an event. A live readout from inside one. Speeds, temperatures, driver numbers, corner by corner.

Guests are never named. They are Driver 04 and Driver 17. That is what lets an invite-only day live in public: nobody's guest list goes out, but everything that happens on track does.

And because it is a readout rather than a recap, the audience has something to answer, guess and vote on all weekend.

02

Before the day

Two stories. That is the whole build up. No announcement, no explanation, just the circuit and a clock running down on it.

Friday 2 October

The club circuit and its eight corners, with one question over it. No date, no venue, nothing to explain what it is.

Thursday 8 October

The night before, the circuit sits inside the full Autodrome map and a countdown sticker goes on. Anyone curious gets pinged by Instagram on the day rather than by us.

03

How we post

Not a live feed. Batches, each one a small sequence with a beginning and an end, so the day reads as chapters rather than as noise. In between, we are shooting.

04

Day one

The day as the audience will follow it, moment by moment, with what goes out and what we are quietly collecting for the film afterwards.

How to read this

Everything below is a guide, not a checklist. It is there so we know what to look for and where to be, but the day will decide what actually gets made. Some of it will be better than what is written here, some of it will not happen at all, and that is the point of shooting live rather than to a shot list.

For reference

The BMW 7 Series launch

One night, one venue, shot the same way we would shoot this. A different world visually, warmer and slower, but the approach is the same: shoot past things rather than at them, let the room and the branding do the work, never pose anyone.

05

Day two

Day two does not repeat day one, and it is a different room. Friday is owners and guests, Saturday is media and creators, so the people coverage moves here where the faces carry further. It also spends the footage nobody has seen yet.

02SATURDAY10 OctoberMedia and creators
06

Resharing guests

A hundred people with phones will out-shoot us every hour of both days. Two ways it comes back, both templated, so whatever they post looks like it came from the same place.

Their stories

Story reshare

Every guest story that tags us goes back out inside one of these, within minutes, all weekend.

Their posts

In-feed reshare

Reels, stills and carousels guests publish themselves, brought back into the same frame so a run of them reads as one event.

07

The sticker set

Animated stickers, free for anyone to use, sitting in the Instagram sticker tray under a MINI search. Guests decorate their own stories with our type and our red without being asked. All drawn from artwork the event already owns.

08

The recap film

Everything in the quiet line under each moment feeds one film the week after. It opens on engine sound before any picture, runs the two days in order, and holds one unbroken readout along the bottom so the whole thing plays like a single lap.
